parsed.explanation: The parent regime imposes tier-1, universal exposures no visitor escapes: passports now reflect birth sex, X markers stopped, entry officers can refuse or flag suspected 'misrepresentation' with lifetime fraud findings, and custody/immigration records document abuse. These are real but contested (courts, suits, several orders enjoined). This state/province adds only documented territory-specific mitigations: working anti-discrimination statutes, constitutional equal-protection coverage, hate-crime law plus hotline, X markers and easy document changes, insurance-mandated gender-affirming care, and correctional protections — placing it in the parent's own low-risk band, though with noted shortfalls in care equity and custody. Per rule 12 it sits above the parent average; the unresolved question of local facility access and the national border/document exposure that still reaches every visitor keep it from the 0.75+ tier.
